main_text.p: mas in homine res præstitisse : optimus orator, optimus imperator, optimus senator. Tamen adversus Numantinos missus, populum unius duntaxat urbis Hispaniæ,Vellei.lib. 2. Appian. de bell. Hispan. eos intra annum tandem ac tres menses, quamvis sexaginta millium exercitu instructus, debellavit. Tu minoribus multo copiis eductis, contra hostes longè potentiores & plures, vix unum mensem abes: & exspectatione videmur nobis falli, quòd victoria celebrem reversum nondum audiamus. Sed qui tam nobili genere, tanta rerum copia, inter tam multas voluptatum illecebras, ita belli aut pacis artibus servieris, ut dignum te præbueris elogioVellei.l.1. Scipionis, Semper inter arma ac studia versatus, aut corpus periculis, aut animum disciplinis exercuit; qui miles in Belgio, Lusitania, Gallia, discrimina non minora, quàmPlutarch. in vita Pauli Æmil. Scipio, subieris; qui imperator missus sis eodem, quò Scipio: ac utinam memineris item eiusFrontin. stratagem. 1.4.c.7. dictum, Imperatorem me mater, non bellatorem peperit; qui denique tuo sanguine, ut Scriptura loquitur,2. Sam.23. 17. quia periculo sanguinis & vitæ, non solùm causam Principis, sed & Dei gloriam, neque patriæ modò pacem, sed Ecclesiæ, defenderis, defendas Scipiones omnes hac ex parte superans, similiorque IosuæIof.9.1. &c

page.notes: Mark a in the text is a superscript letter after "Hispaniæ," and the margin mark is a similar sign; read as a. Marks b to f were matched by position and shape. The initial word "mas" is a fragment carried over from the previous page. The italic spans and the hyphenated "ex-" at the line end (joined as exspectatione) are read from the scan and may need checking. No page number is printed on this page.
